questions.question: Krishna gave \(\dfrac{1}{9}\) th of his savings to his son, \(\dfrac{3}{4}\) th of the remaining to his eldest daughter, and the rest to his second daughter. If the eldest daughter gets Rs. 8800 more than second one, then how much did the son get?
questions.questionHtml: Krishna gave \(\dfrac{1}{9}\)th of his savings to his son, \(\dfrac{3}{4}\)th of the remaining to his eldest daughter, and the rest to his second daughter. If the eldest daughter gets Rs. 8800 more than second one, then how much did the son get?
questions.solution:
Let, total savings of Krishna = 900x and Krishna's son get \({1\over 9}\) × 900x = 100x. Remaining amount of Eldest Daughter = \({3 \over 4}\) × 800x  = 600x.

Remaining amount of second daughter = 800x - 600x = 200x

Now, Eldest Daughter - second daughter = 8800 ⇒ 600x - 200x = 8800 ⇒ x = 22, Hence, Krishna's son get = 100x = Rs. 2200

questions.question: Three different positions of the same non-standard dice are shown. Which number will be on the face opposite to the face with the number '4'?
questions.questionHtml: Three different positions of the same non-standard dice are shown. Which number will be on the face opposite to the face with the number '4'?
questions.solution:
From second and third positions, it is clear that-

'5' is opposite to '6' (As numbers '2', '3', '4' and '1' are adjacent to '6'.)

And from third position, it is observed that-

'1' and '6' are adjacent to '4' ⇒ So, either '2' or '3' can be opposite to face with number '4'. 

Now, assuming that '3' is at the back in the third position, rotate the third position such that '6' is on the front face.

This proves that second position can not be obtained as 2 will not be on the right face.

So, in third position, number '3' is not at the back, it is on the left face.

And as '4' is on the right face, so '3' and '4' are opposite to each other.

Hence, number '3' is opposite to the face with the number '4'.

A minister of the state lied about some facts on live TV for protecting government.

Course of actions:

questions.solution:
The logic followed is:

In the given statement: For the sake of defending the administration, a state minister lied about several facts on live television.

As a minister of a state, the minister is responsible to the public of the state. So, if a minister lied to the people then legal actions should be taken against him.

Therefore, only course of action I) follows.

Hence, the correct answer is Option 4).

Additional Information

Some rules to solve Statements and Course of action questions must be kept in mind while solving it.

Rule 1. Have an unbiased and neutral mind frame. Individual perception must not be used to judge the course of action to be taken.

Rule 2. The first step should be to identify the root cause of the problem. Once the problem is solved, a logical mindset should be employed to figure out the course of action.

Rule 3. There must be no extremity involved in the course of action.

Rule 4. A course of action must be able to solve, reduce, or minimize the problem given in the situation.

Rule 5. The course of action can be said to solve/reduce the problem when it is an established fact, when it is logically possible and when it is known from experience.

questions.question: A shopkeeper buys a product for Rs.80 and marks a price assuming a profit of 50% on his cost price. At the time of making the sale, he gives a 20% discount on the marked price. What is the amount of net profit he makes on this product?
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper buys a product for Rs.80 and marks a price assuming a profit of 50% on his cost price. At the time of making the sale, he gives a 20% discount on the marked price. What is the amount of net profit he makes on this product?
questions.solution:
CP of product = Rs.80

Markup% = 50% (As he marks a price assuming a profit of 50% on CP)

So, Marked Price = Rs.80 + 50% of Rs.80

                             = Rs.80 + Rs.40 

                             = Rs.120

Discount% = 20% 

So, Selling Price = Marked Price - Discount

                            = Rs.120 - 20% of Rs.120

                            = Rs.120 - Rs.24

                            = Rs.96

Net Profit = SP - CP

                = Rs.96 - Rs.80

                = Rs.16

Hence, Net Profit = Rs.16

MarkUp% = 50% 

Discount% = 20%

So, Profit% = 50 - 20 - (50 × 20) / 100

                   = 50 - 20 -10

       Profit% = 20%

Profit% = 20%

CP = Rs.80 

20 × 80 = Profit × 100

Profit = 1600 ÷ 100

         = Rs.16

Hence, Net Profit = Rs.16

• When a large force acts on a body for a short time, then the force is called impulsive force.

  • Impulse is a vector quantity.
  • SI Unit of Impulse is Newton second (Ns).

Impulse

  • An impulsive force does not remain constant, but changes first from zero to maximum and then from maximum to zero. In such a case, we measure the total effect of force.

questions.question: Which of the following measures the magnitude of an earthquake?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following measures the magnitude of an earthquake?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Richter scale.

Key Points

  • The Richter scale is a logarithmic scale used to measure the magnitude of earthquakes.
  • It was developed in 1935 by Charles F. Richter, a seismologist, in collaboration with Beno Gutenberg.
  • The scale quantifies the amount of energy released during an earthquake.
  • It is based on measurements of the amplitude of seismic waves recorded by a seismograph.
  • The scale is logarithmic, meaning each whole number increase represents a tenfold increase in amplitude and approximately 31.6 times more energy release.
  • The Richter scale is suitable for measuring the magnitude of small to medium earthquakes but is not as effective for very large earthquakes.
  • This scale is essential for seismologists to assess the intensity of an earthquake and its potential impact.

Additional Information

  • Explanation of Other Options:
    • Polygraph: Also known as a lie detector, it measures physiological responses such as heart rate, blood pressure, and respiration to assess truthfulness. It is not related to earthquake measurement.
    • Barometer: This instrument is used to measure atmospheric pressure. It is commonly used in weather forecasting but has no connection to earthquake magnitude.
    • Thermometer: A thermometer measures temperature, whether it is of the environment, human body, or any other system. It is irrelevant to seismology.
  • Richter Scale Characteristics:
    • The scale ranges from 1 to 10, where values below 2 are typically not felt by humans, and values above 7 represent major earthquakes with potential for significant destruction.
    • The largest earthquake ever recorded on the Richter scale was the 1960 Valdivia earthquake in Chile, with a magnitude of 9.5.
  • Modern Advances:
    • While the Richter scale is historically significant, modern seismologists use the Moment Magnitude Scale (Mw), which provides more accurate measurements of large earthquakes.
    • Both scales are logarithmic and are consistent for small to medium earthquakes.

Important Points

  • Seismographs:
    • These instruments are used to record seismic waves generated by earthquakes.
    • Seismographs detect ground motion and create a visual representation called a seismogram.
  • Earthquake Preparedness:
    • Knowing the magnitude and location of an earthquake helps in disaster management and preparedness.
    • Countries like Japan and the United States have advanced seismic monitoring systems to mitigate earthquake-related risks.

questions.question: Who among the following is known as the Father of the Communal Electorate in India?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following is known as the Father of the Communal Electorate in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lord Minto.

Key Points

  • Lord Minto, who served as the Viceroy of India from 1905 to 1910, is regarded as the "Father of the Communal Electorate" in India.
  • The concept of communal electorates was introduced in the Indian Councils Act of 1909, also known as the Morley-Minto Reforms.
  • This reform allowed separate electorates for Muslims, where only Muslims could vote for Muslim candidates in designated constituencies.
  • The idea aimed to address the political representation of Muslims in India but eventually led to the politicization of religious identities.
  • The introduction of communal electorates sowed the seeds of division between Hindus and Muslims, which later became a significant factor in India's partition.

Additional Information

  • Lord Morley:
    • Lord Morley was the Secretary of State for India during the Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909.
    • He played a significant role in drafting the reforms, which introduced limited constitutional changes, including the communal electorates.
    • Although he worked closely with Lord Minto, Morley's role was more administrative and policy-focused rather than direct involvement in India.
  • Lord Chelmsford:
    • Lord Chelmsford served as the Viceroy of India from 1916 to 1921.
    • He is best known for the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms of 1919, which introduced the system of dyarchy in provincial governance.
    • These reforms expanded the scope of Indian representation but did not introduce communal electorates.
  • Lord Metcalfe:
    • Lord Metcalfe was the acting Governor-General of India from 1835 to 1836.
    • He is remembered for his efforts to promote press freedom in India by repealing restrictions on the press.
    • His contributions are unrelated to the concept of communal electorates or constitutional reforms.

questions.question: The magnificent temple at Gangaikonda Cholapuram was commissioned by which Chola ruler?
questions.questionHtml: The magnificent temple at Gangaikonda Cholapuram was commissioned by which Chola ruler?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Rajendra Chola I.

Key Points

  • The magnificent temple at Gangaikonda Cholapuram was commissioned by Rajendra Chola I, a ruler of the Chola dynasty in South India.
  • Rajendra Chola I was the son and successor of Rajaraja Chola I, who was also a great temple builder.
  • The temple was built to commemorate Rajendra Chola I's victories in Northern India, particularly his successful campaign to bring the waters of the Ganges to his kingdom.
  • Gangaikonda Cholapuram was established as the capital of the Chola empire during the reign of Rajendra Chola I, replacing Thanjavur.
  • The temple is an architectural marvel and is part of the group of Great Living Chola Temples, which are recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
  • The temple is known for its massive vimana (tower) and intricate carvings that reflect the artistic and cultural brilliance of the Chola dynasty.

Additional Information

  • Rajendra Chola I:
    • Rajendra Chola I ruled from 1014 CE to 1044 CE and is considered one of the greatest rulers of the Chola dynasty.
    • He expanded the Chola empire to its greatest extent, covering parts of present-day India, Sri Lanka, Maldives, Malaysia, and Indonesia.
    • Rajendra Chola I is also credited with establishing a strong naval force, enabling the Cholas to dominate maritime trade and politics in the Indian Ocean region.
  • Gangaikonda Cholapuram Temple:
    • The temple is an example of Dravidian architecture, featuring exquisite sculptures and carvings.
    • The temple's vimana (tower) is slightly shorter than the Brihadeshwara Temple in Thanjavur but is more intricately designed.
    • The temple was dedicated to Lord Shiva and houses a massive Shiva Lingam in its sanctum.
    • The bronze sculptures and stone carvings in the temple depict scenes from Hindu mythology and reflect the artistic advancements of the Chola period.
  • Great Living Chola Temples:
    • The group includes three temples: Brihadeshwara Temple at Thanjavur, Gangaikonda Cholapuram Temple, and Airavatesvara Temple at Darasuram.
    • These temples were recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987 due to their architectural and cultural significance.
  • Other Rulers of the Chola Dynasty:
    • Rajaraja Chola I: Known for building the Brihadeshwara Temple in Thanjavur.
    • Rajadhiraja Chola I: Successor of Rajendra Chola I, who continued the military campaigns and architectural endeavors of the Chola dynasty.
    • Kulothunga Chola I: Known for consolidating the Chola empire and fostering trade relations with Southeast Asia.

Important Points

  • The Chola dynasty is renowned for its contributions to art, architecture, and administration.
  • Their temple architecture, especially the use of granite and intricate carvings, set a benchmark in South Indian architecture.
  • The Chola kings were great patrons of Shaivism, and their temples often featured grand Shiva Lingams and elaborately designed sanctums.
  • The Chola dynasty also excelled in maritime trade, with ports such as Nagapattinam and Poompuhar serving as key trade hubs.

questions.question: Which organelle is called the 'suicidal bag' of the cell?
questions.questionHtml: Which organelle is called the 'suicidal bag' of the cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lysosome.

Key Points

  • Lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles found in eukaryotic cells, often referred to as the "suicidal bag" of the cell because they contain powerful hydrolytic enzymes capable of digesting cellular components.
  • They play a crucial role in intracellular digestion, breaking down macromolecules such as proteins, lipids, carbohydrates, and nucleic acids.
  • Lysosomes are involved in the process of autophagy, wherein they degrade damaged or unnecessary organelles to maintain cellular health.
  • If lysosomes rupture or their enzymes are released uncontrollably, it can lead to self-destruction of the cell, hence the term "suicidal bag."
  • Lysosomal enzymes function optimally in an acidic environment (pH ~5), which is maintained by proton pumps on the lysosomal membrane.

Additional Information

  • Functions of Lysosomes:
    • Phagocytosis: Lysosomes fuse with phagosomes to digest pathogens or foreign particles engulfed by the cell.
    • Autophagy: Lysosomes degrade damaged organelles, such as mitochondria, and recycle their components.
    • Exocytosis: In some cells, lysosomes release their contents outside the cell, aiding in processes like bone resorption by osteoclasts.
  • Discovery: Lysosomes were first discovered by Belgian biochemist Christian de Duve in 1955. He won the Nobel Prize in 1974 for his contributions to cell biology.
  • Structure: Lysosomes are surrounded by a single lipid bilayer membrane that protects the cell from the hydrolytic enzymes they contain.
  • Diseases Associated with Lysosomes:
    • Lysosomal storage diseases, such as Tay-Sachs disease and Gaucher's disease, result from the deficiency of specific lysosomal enzymes.
    • These diseases lead to the accumulation of undigested substrates within lysosomes, causing cellular dysfunction.
  • Comparison with Other Organelles:
    • Mitochondria: Known as the "powerhouse" of the cell, mitochondria generate energy in the form of ATP but do not participate in digestion.
    • Golgi Body: Responsible for packaging and modifying proteins, it works alongside lysosomes by tagging enzymes for lysosomal transport.
    • Ribosomes: Sites of protein synthesis; they do not contain enzymes for digestion.

Important Points

  • Hydrolytic Enzymes: Lysosomes contain enzymes like proteases, lipases, nucleases, and carbohydrases that enable the breakdown of complex molecules.
  • pH Dependency: Lysosomal enzymes require an acidic environment to function effectively, differentiating them from enzymes in other organelles.
  • Role in Immunity: Lysosomes help destroy pathogens engulfed by immune cells like macrophages.
  • Autolysis: Lysosomes play a role in programmed cell death, releasing enzymes to dismantle cellular components during apoptosis.

  • Role of Emperor Ashoka:
    • Ashoka embraced Buddhism after the Kalinga War and became a patron of the religion.
    • He commissioned numerous stupas and pillars across India to spread the teachings of Buddha.
    • The original structure at Sarnath, built during Ashoka's reign, was later replaced by the Dhamek Stupa in 500 CE.

questions.questionHtml: The value of \(\frac{6.25+\frac{6}{7}\:of\:21-3}{\frac{3}{4}\:of(15.8-3.4)+5\times2.39}\) is:
questions.solution:
Given:

\(\frac{6.25 + \frac{6}{7} \times 21 - 3}{\frac{3}{4} \times (15.8 - 3.4) + 5 \times 2.39}\)

Formula used:

BODMAS rule (Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

Calculation:

questions.question: A and B together can finish a work in 20 days. If they worked together for 8 days, then what was the share of work that was yet to be completed?
questions.questionHtml: A and B together can finish a work in 20 days. If they worked together for 8 days, then what was the share of work that was yet to be completed?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total time taken by A and B to complete the work = 20 days.

Part of the work completed by them in 1 day = 1/20.

Part of the work completed by them in 8 days = 8 × (1/20) = 2/5.

Share of remaining work = 1 − 2/5 = 3/5.

∴ The correct answer is 3/5.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by A and B together to complete the work = 20 days.

Number of days they worked together = 8 days.

Formula Used:

Work Done = Efficiency × Time

Remaining Work Fraction = Remaining Work ÷ Total Work

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
A + B 20 20 1

Calculations:

⇒ Total work = 20 units (LCM of 20)

⇒ Combined efficiency of A and B = 1 unit/day

⇒ Work completed by A and B in 8 days = 8 × 1 = 8 units

⇒ Remaining work = Total work − Completed work

⇒ Remaining work = 20 − 8 = 12 units

⇒ Share of work yet to be completed = 12 ÷ 20 = 3/5

∴ The correct answer is 3/5.

Additional Information

Pipes and Cisterns

Similar to time and work, an inlet pipe's work is considered positive, while an outlet pipe's work (leak) is considered negative.

Work and Wages

Wages are distributed in proportion to the total work done by each individual. If they work for the same number of days, wages are distributed in the ratio of their individual efficiencies.

Alternate Day Work

When individuals work on alternate days, find the combined work done in a specific cycle of days (e.g., 2 days) and calculate cycles required to reach the total work.

questions.question: Cost of four chairs is equal to cost of two tables. Cost of four tables is equal to cost of two boards and cost of four boards is equal to cost of two fans. If a fan costs ₹850, then the cost of a chair is:
questions.questionHtml: Cost of four chairs is equal to cost of two tables. Cost of four tables is equal to cost of two boards and cost of four boards is equal to cost of two fans. If a fan costs ₹850, then the cost of a chair is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

By equating the costs given in the problem, we establish a direct chain:

1 Fan = 2 Boards = 4 Tables = 8 Chairs

Cost of 1 Fan = ₹850

Cost of 8 Chairs = ₹850

Cost of 1 Chair = 850 ÷ 8 = ₹106.25

∴ The correct answer is ₹106.25.

Alternate Method

Given:

Cost of 4 chairs = Cost of 2 tables

Cost of 4 tables = Cost of 2 boards

Cost of 4 boards = Cost of 2 fans

Cost of 1 fan = ₹850

Calculations:

Let the cost of a chair, table, board, and fan be C, T, B, and F respectively.

⇒ 4C = 2T ⇒ T = 2C

⇒ 4T = 2B ⇒ B = 2T

⇒ 4B = 2F ⇒ F = 2B

Substituting T and B in terms of C:

⇒ B = 2 × (2C) = 4C

⇒ F = 2 × (4C) = 8C

We are given that the cost of 1 Fan (F) = ₹850

⇒ 8C = 850

⇒ C = 850 ÷ 8

⇒ C = 106.25

∴ The correct answer is ₹106.25.

Additional Information

Unitary Method

Finding the value of a single unit from a multiple and then using it to find the value of desired units is the core principle used in solving continuous equivalence equations.

Compound Ratio

When multiple ratios like a:b, b:c, and c:d are given, their compound relationship can be found by multiplying the individual ratios: (a/b) × (b/c) × (c/d).

questions.question: A businessman marks his goods 20% more than their cost price. By giving a certain discount he suffers a loss of 4%. What percentage discount did he give?
questions.questionHtml: A businessman marks his goods 20% more than their cost price. By giving a certain discount he suffers a loss of 4%. What percentage discount did he give?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let the Cost Price (CP) of the goods be 100.

Marked Price (MP) = 100 + 20% of 100 = 120.

Selling Price (SP) = 100 − 4% of 100 = 96.

Discount = MP − SP = 120 − 96 = 24.

Discount Percentage = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100 = (24 ÷ 120) × 100 = 20%.

∴ The correct answer is 20%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Markup Percentage = 20%

Loss Percentage = 4%

Formula Used:

MP ÷ CP = (100 − Loss %) ÷ (100 − Discount %)

Calculation:

Let CP be 100.

⇒ MP = 100 × (120 ÷ 100) = 120

⇒ 120 ÷ 100 = (100 − 4) ÷ (100 − Discount %)

⇒ 1.2 = 96 ÷ (100 − Discount %)

⇒ 100 − Discount % = 96 ÷ 1.2

⇒ 100 − Discount % = 80

⇒ Discount % = 100 − 80 = 20%

∴ The correct answer is 20%.

Additional Information

Marked Price (MP) and Cost Price (CP) Relation

The ratio of Marked Price to Cost Price can be directly calculated using the formula: MP ÷ CP = (100 ± Profit/Loss %) ÷ (100 − Discount %).

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount is given by: (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a dealer claims to sell at the cost price but uses a false weight, the actual Profit % is calculated as: (True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight × 100.

questions.question: If x is the mean proportional between 39 and 156 and y is the third proportional to 24 and 36, then for 6x ∶ 13y = ?
questions.questionHtml: If x is the mean proportional between 39 and 156 and y is the third proportional to 24 and 36, then for 6x ∶ 13y = ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Mean proportional x = √(39 × 156) = √(39 × 39 × 4) = 78

Third proportional y = 362 ÷ 24 = 1296 ÷ 24 = 54

Ratio 6x : 13y = (6 × 78) : (13 × 54)

Ratio = 468 : 702 = 2 : 3

∴ The correct answer is 2 : 3.

Alternate Method

Given:

⇒ Mean proportional x is between 39 and 156.

⇒ Third proportional y is to 24 and 36.

Formula Used:

⇒ Mean proportional between a and b = √(a × b)

⇒ Third proportional to a and b is c, where c = b2 ÷ a

Calculations:

⇒ Mean proportional x = √(39 × 156)

⇒ x = √(39 × 39 × 4)

⇒ x = 39 × 2 = 78

⇒ Third proportional y = 362 ÷ 24

⇒ y = (36 × 36) ÷ 24 = 1296 ÷ 24 = 54

⇒ We need to calculate 6x : 13y

⇒ 6x : 13y = (6 × 78) : (13 × 54)

⇒ 6x : 13y = 468 : 702

⇒ Dividing both values by their common factor 234

⇒ 6x : 13y = 2 : 3

∴ The correct answer is 2 : 3.

Additional Information

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is √(ab). It is the middle term x in the continuous proportion a : x :: x : b.

Third Proportional

The third proportional to two numbers a and b is c, given by the relation a : b = b : c. Simplifying this gives c = b2 ÷ a.

Fourth Proportional

The fourth proportional to three numbers a, b, and c is d, where a : b = c : d. Solving for d gives d = (b × c) ÷ a.

questions.questionHtml: A cylindrical tube open at both ends is made of metal. The internal diameter of tube is 11.2 cm and its length is 21 cm. The metal everywhere is 0.4 cm thick. The volume of the metal \(\left( {Take\;\pi = \frac{{22}}{7}} \right)\) is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Internal radius (r) = 11.2 ÷ 2 = 5.6 cm, External radius (R) = 5.6 + 0.4 = 6.0 cm

Volume of metal = π × h × (R + r)(R − r)

Volume = (22/7) × 21 × (6 + 5.6)(6 − 5.6)

Volume = 66 × 11.6 × 0.4 = 306.24 cm3

∴ The correct answer is 306.24 cm3.

Alternate Method

Given:

Internal diameter = 11.2 cm

Thickness = 0.4 cm

Height (h) = 21 cm

Formula Used:

Volume of metal in hollow cylinder = π × h × (R2 − r2)

Calculations:

⇒ Internal radius (r) = 11.2 ÷ 2 = 5.6 cm

⇒ External radius (R) = 5.6 + 0.4 = 6.0 cm

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × 21 × (6.02 − 5.62)

⇒ Volume = 22 × 3 × (36 − 31.36)

⇒ Volume = 66 × 4.64

⇒ Volume = 306.24 cm3

∴ The correct answer is 306.24 cm3.

Additional Information

Volume of Hollow Cylinder

Volume = πh(R2 − r2), where R is external radius, r is internal radius, and h is height.

Curved Surface Area (CSA)

CSA of a hollow cylinder is the sum of the inner and outer curved surfaces: 2πRh + 2πrh = 2πh(R + r).

Total Surface Area (TSA)

TSA of a hollow cylinder includes both curved surfaces and the area of the two ring-shaped bases: 2πh(R + r) + 2π(R2 − r2).

questions.question: The CP of an article is Rs. 7,000. By selling it, a person gains 10%. How much should the person sell it for to get a gain of Rs. 50 more?
questions.questionHtml: The CP of an article is Rs. 7,000. By selling it, a person gains 10%. How much should the person sell it for to get a gain of Rs. 50 more?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Initial Profit = 10% of 7000 = Rs. 700

Required New Profit = Initial Profit + 50 = 700 + 50 = Rs. 750

New Selling Price = CP + New Profit = 7000 + 750 = Rs. 7750

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 7,750.

Alternate Method

Given:

Cost Price (CP) = Rs. 7,000

Initial Gain = 10%

Extra Gain required = Rs. 50

Formula Used:

Gain = (Gain% ÷ 100) × CP

Selling Price (SP) = CP + Total Gain

Calculations:

⇒ Initial Gain = (10 ÷ 100) × 7000

⇒ Initial Gain = Rs. 700

⇒ Total Gain required = Initial Gain + 50

⇒ Total Gain = 700 + 50 = Rs. 750

⇒ New Selling Price = CP + Total Gain

⇒ New Selling Price = 7000 + 750 = Rs. 7750

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 7,750.

Additional Information

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit occurs when Selling Price (SP) is greater than the Cost Price (CP). Profit = SP − CP.

Profit Percentage

Profit % is always calculated on the base Cost Price unless stated otherwise. Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Selling Price Formula

To calculate the Selling Price directly with the gain percentage: SP = CP × (100 + Gain%) ÷ 100.

questions.question: Avi runs at 16km/hr and Vikas runs at 25% more speed than Avi towards each other. What was the distance between them when they started if they meet after 1 hr12 minutes?
questions.questionHtml: Avi runs at 16km/hr and Vikas runs at 25% more speed than Avi towards each other. What was the distance between them when they started if they meet after 1 hr12 minutes?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Speed of Avi = 16 km/hr.

Speed of Vikas = 16 + (25% of 16) = 16 + 4 = 20 km/hr.

Since they run towards each other, their relative speed = 16 + 20 = 36 km/hr.

Total time taken = 1 hr 12 min = 1 + (12 ÷ 60) hr = 1.2 hours.

Total initial distance = Relative speed × Time = 36 × 1.2 = 43.2 km.

∴ The correct answer is 43.2 km.

Alternate Method

Given:

Speed of Avi = 16 km/hr

Speed of Vikas is 25% more than Avi.

Time after which they meet = 1 hr 12 minutes.

Formula Used:

Relative Speed (when moving in opposite directions) = S1 + S2

Distance = Speed × Time

Calculations:

⇒ Speed of Vikas = 16 + (25 ÷ 100) × 16

⇒ Speed of Vikas = 16 + 4 = 20 km/hr

⇒ Relative Speed = Speed of Avi + Speed of Vikas

⇒ Relative Speed = 16 + 20 = 36 km/hr

⇒ Time taken = 1 hour + 12 minutes = 1 + (12 ÷ 60) hours = 1 + (1 ÷ 5) = 1.2 hours

⇒ Total Distance = Relative Speed × Time

⇒ Total Distance = 36 × 1.2 = 43.2 km

∴ The correct answer is 43.2 km.

Additional Information

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (S1 − S2).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply the given speed by 5/18. To convert m/s back to km/hr, multiply the speed by 18/5.

Average Speed

When a certain distance is covered at speed x and the exact equal return distance is covered at speed y, the average speed for the entire journey is calculated as (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

questions.questionHtml: If \({tanθ+cotθ}\over{tanθ-cotθ}\) = 2, then find the value of θ =?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

By applying the Componendo and Dividendo rule:

tanθ / cotθ = (2 + 1) / (2 − 1)

tan2θ = 3

tanθ = √3 ⇒ θ = 60°

∴ The correct answer is 60°.

Alternate Method

Given:

(tanθ + cotθ) / (tanθ − cotθ) = 2

Calculations:

By cross-multiplying the given equation:

⇒ tanθ + cotθ = 2 × (tanθ − cotθ)

⇒ tanθ + cotθ = 2tanθ − 2cotθ

Bringing similar terms to one side:

⇒ 2cotθ + cotθ = 2tanθ − tanθ

⇒ 3cotθ = tanθ

We know that cotθ = 1 / tanθ, substituting this back into the equation:

⇒ 3 × (1 / tanθ) = tanθ

⇒ 3 = tan2θ

⇒ tanθ = √3

Since tan 60° = √3:

⇒ θ = 60°

∴ The correct answer is 60°.

Additional Information

Componendo and Dividendo Rule

If a / b = c / d, then (a + b) / (a − b) = (c + d) / (c − d). This rule is highly useful for simplifying rational fractions in algebra and trigonometry.

Important Trigonometric Values

tan 30° = 1 / √3, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3, tan 90° = Undefined.

Reciprocal Identities

tanθ and cotθ are reciprocals of each other. Therefore, tanθ × cotθ = 1 and cotθ = 1 / tanθ.

= (8 × 7) × 6 + (4 × 7) × (3 × 5) + 8 × (5 × 4) + (3 × 5) = 931

questions.question: If the elevation of the Sun changed from 30° to 60°, then the difference between the lengths of shadows of a pole 15m high is:
questions.questionHtml: If the elevation of the Sun changed from 30° to 60°, then the difference between the lengths of shadows of a pole 15m high is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Direct formula for the difference in shadow lengths: d = h × (cot θ1 − cot θ2)

Given: Height (h) = 15 m, θ1 = 30°, θ2 = 60°

⇒ d = 15 × (cot 30° − cot 60°)

⇒ d = 15 × (√3 − 1/√3) = 15 × (2 / √3)

⇒ d = 30 / √3 = 10√3 m

∴ The correct answer is 10√3 m.

Alternate Method

Given:

Height of the pole (AB) = 15 m

Angles of elevation of the Sun = 30° and 60°

Calculations:

Let the lengths of the shadows be BC and BD for the angles 60° and 30° respectively.

⇒ In right-angled ΔABC:

⇒ tan 60° = AB ÷ BC

⇒ √3 = 15 ÷ BC

⇒ BC = 15 ÷ √3 = 5√3 m

⇒ In right-angled ΔABD:

⇒ tan 30° = AB ÷ BD

⇒ 1/√3 = 15 ÷ BD

⇒ BD = 15√3 m

⇒ Difference in lengths of shadows (CD) = BD − BC

⇒ CD = 15√3 − 5√3 = 10√3 m

∴ The correct answer is 10√3 m.

Additional Information

Angle of Elevation

It is the angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when an object is placed above the horizontal level.

Angle of Depression

It is the angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when an object is placed below the horizontal level.

Trigonometric Values

tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3

questions.question: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 400 metres. When the policeman starts to chase the thief also starts running. If the speed of the thief is18 km/h and that of the policeman 20 km/h, then how far would the thief have run before he is overtaken?
questions.questionHtml: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 400 metres. When the policeman starts to chase the thief also starts running. If the speed of the thief is18 km/h and that of the policeman 20 km/h, then how far would the thief have run before he is overtaken?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of speeds (Thief : Policeman) = 18 : 20 = 9 : 10

Since time is constant, the ratio of distances covered = 9 : 10

Difference in ratio parts = 10 − 9 = 1 part

1 part represents the initial gap = 400 m

Distance run by the thief = 9 parts = 9 × 400 m = 3600 m = 3.6 km

∴ The correct answer is 3.6 km.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial distance between them = 400 m = 0.4 km

Speed of thief = 18 km/h

Speed of policeman = 20 km/h

Formula Used:

Relative Speed = Speed of Policeman − Speed of Thief

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Distance = Speed × Time

Calculations:

⇒ Relative speed = 20 − 18 = 2 km/h

⇒ Time taken to overtake = 0.4 km ÷ 2 km/h = 0.2 hours

⇒ Distance run by the thief = Speed of thief × Time taken

⇒ Distance run by the thief = 18 km/h × 0.2 hours = 3.6 km

∴ The correct answer is 3.6 km.

Additional Information

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds (S1 − S2).

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two bodies move towards each other in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S1 + S2).

Constant Time Concept

If the time of travel is the same for two moving objects, the ratio of the distance covered by them is exactly equal to the ratio of their respective speeds (D1 : D2 = S1 : S2).

questions.question: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: (1) If one wishes to truly understand the philosophical underpinnings of the Enlightenment, / (2) one shall be prepared to delve into the dense and often contradictory writings / (3) of both the French Encyclopedists and the British empiricists / (4) who shaped the intellectual landscape in the eighteenth century.

  • Correction: The sentence should read: "...one must be prepared to delve..." or "...one should be prepared to delve..."

  • आइए दिए गए विकल्पों के अर्थ देखें:

  • उदाहरण:

Key Points

  • The given sentence is in the Passive Voice. As per the given question we have to change the sentence into Active Form. 
  • The process of transformation of these kinds of sentences as follows:
    • Subject + modal + have + V3 + object. (Active Voice)
    • Object + modal + have + been + V3 + by + Subject. (Passive Voice)
  • Example:
    • She will have delivered the letter. (Active Voice)
    • The letter will have been delivered by her. (Passive Voice) 
  • The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject. 
  • 'ought to have been respected' will be changed into 'ought to have respected'. 
  • Lastly, the preposition 'by' will be removed. 
  • Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is Option 3. 
    ​

Correct Sentence: The students ought to have respected the teachers. 

  • दी गई वाक्य Passive voice में है। दिए गए प्रश्न के अनुसार, हमें वाक्य को Active voice में बदलना होगा ।
  • इस प्रकार के वाक्यों के परिवर्तन की प्रक्रिया निम्नानुसार है:
    • Subject + modal + have + V3 + object. (Active Voice)
    • Object + modal + have + been + V3 + by + Subject. (Passive Voice)
  • Subject Object के स्थान पर रखा जाएगा और Object को Subject के स्थान पर रखा जाएगा ।
  • 'ought to have been respected' को 'ought to have respected' में बदल दिया जाएगा ।
  • अंत में, 'By' preposition हटा दिया जाएगा।

Select the most appropriate ANTONYM for the bracketed word:
In the ceremony, the artist was excited to (unveil) his latest masterpiece.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Conceal'.

Key Points

  • The given word is 'Unveil'. It means to remove a cover or curtain from a painting or statue, so that it can be seen by others. Its Hindi translation is 'अनावरण करना' (Anavaran Karna).
    • Example: The museum will unveil its new exhibit next week.
  • The correct antonym to fill in the blank is 'Conceal'. It refers to keep from sight; hide. Its Hindi translation is 'छुपाना' (Chupana).
    • Example: She tried to conceal the fact that she had been crying.

Therefore, the correct answer is 'option 1'.

Additional Information

  • The word 'Champion' (Option 2) means to support, defend, or fight for a person, belief, right, or principle enthusiastically. Its Hindi translation is 'चैम्पियन' (Champion).
  • The word 'Expand' (Option 3) refers to the act of becoming or making something become larger in size, volume, quantity, or scope. Its Hindi translation is 'विस्तार करना' (Vistar Karna).
  • The word 'Widen' (Option 4) means to make or become more broad or extensive. Its Hindi translation is 'चौड़ा करना' (Choda Karna).

Key Points

  • The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Present Perfect Continuous Tense.
  • Therefore, when converting to Indirect Speech, the sentence should be in Past Perfect Continuous Tense. This aligns with the rule in English grammar that states we should always convert the verbs back one step in time in indirect speech.
  • The rule for this conversion is: Present Perfect Continuous (Subject + has/have been + Present Participle + Object) should be converted into Past Perfect Continuous (Subject + had been + Present Participle + Object).
  • Hence, "I've been thinking" becomes "she had been thinking" and "it's", which is short for "it is", becomes "it was" in the reported speech.

Therefore, the correct answer is- 'Option 2'

 Additional Information

  • The problem with option 1 is that "has been thinking" is in the present perfect continuous tense, which is incorrect because it doesn't match the past context.
  • Option 3 changes the meaning of the statement to future tense ("she would think about the book") which deviates from the original direct speech where she has already thought about the book.
  • Option 4 has the correct tense change but the positioning of "last weekend" at the end of the sentence is awkward and can cause confusion. The time phrase is best located at the beginning of the sentence for clarity. Therefore, Option B remains the best choice.

questions.question: Complete the sentence using appropriate option The crowd that ______ due to the quarrel has dispersed now.
questions.questionHtml: Complete the sentence using appropriate option The crowd that ______ due to the quarrel has dispersed now.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 3' - had gathered.

 Key Points

  • The phrase "had gathered" is in the past perfect tense.
  • Past perfect tense is used when two actions happened in the past and one action occurred before the other.
  • In this sentence, the first action is the crowd gathering (which was in the past), and the next action is the crowd dispersing.
  • Therefore, we use "had gathered" to denote that the gathering happened first, and afterwards, it dispersed.

Therefore, the correct answer is- 'Option 3' - had gathered.

 Additional Information

  • have gathered (Option 1): This is in the present perfect tense and is inappropriate as we are talking about two past actions.
  • has been gathered (Option 2): This passive form in the present perfect tense is inappropriate as the crowd gathered by themselves due to the quarrel.
  • has been gathering (Option 4): This present perfect continuous tense refers to an action that began in the past and still continues, which is not applicable in this case.

questions.questionHtml:
This question consists of six sentences of a passage. The first and sixth sentences are given in the beginning as S1 and S6. The middle four sentences have been jumbled up and labelled as P, Q, R and S. Rearrange the sentences and choose the correct option.

S1: Printing is a device for multiplying what is written by making copies of it.
S6: So far as Europe is concerned, the type was first used in Holland.
P: Little metal letters called type, are arranged in such a way as to form the words that you want to print.
Q: The inked letters leave their marks upon the paper and these marks are the printed words.
R: The letters are then inked over and sheets of paper are pressed down tight upon them.
S: As many copies can be made of what is printed as there are sheets of paper.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is- 'PRQS.' Key Points 

  • By reading the above-given options we can understand that the paragraph is about printers.
  • Part R will follow part P, as the adverb 'then' suggests that the noun 'letters' has already been introduced by a previous sentence.
  • Q will follow next, as the noun 'inked letters' was introduced in part R.
  • The only option left is part S, thus it will come last.
  • Thus option 4 is the correct answer.

The correct sequence is:
S1: Printing is a device for multiplying what is written by making copies of it.
P: Little metal letters called type, are arranged in such a way as to form the words that you want to print.
R: The letters are then inked over and sheets of paper are pressed down tight upon them.
Q: The inked letters leave their marks upon the paper and these marks are the printed words.
S: As many copies can be made of what is printed as there are sheets of paper.
S6: So far as Europe is concerned, the type was first used in Holland. Important Points   

  • Here are some tips to solve the para jumbles:
    • You need to understand the idea behind the paragraph. If you can understand the idea/theme of the paragraph it is easy to put the sentences in order then.
    • You should look out for the starting or the concluding sentences in the question. Sometimes they are clearly visible and can help you immensely in identifying the correct sequence.
    • You need to know the relationships between different sentences to put them in the right sequence. 
    • You should first fix the relationships of sentences, put them in order and then check the options.
    • Transition words and contrasting words also help in finding clean relationships between sentences of the sentence rearrangement.
    • Do not over depend on options, they only confuse you if you keep looking at them, use them as facilitators only, especially to fix your first sentence.
    • The whole paragraph should have a coherent idea and flow when arranged in the correct order.
